no_target_yet.statement:
Every two-qubit density matrix satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \F(\rho)\leq\max\{\sqrt{3(1-c_B)},1\}.
\end{equation}
For every real $0\leq t<2/3$ there is a two-qubit density matrix with
$c_B=t$ and $\F>1$. Consequently the centre lengths supporting a
violation are exactly $[0,2/3)$.

The corrected form of Result~2 of~\cite{DSS} is
\[
 c_B\geq2/3\ \Longrightarrow\ \HF{A}(\rho)\leq1,
 \qquad
c_A\geq2/3\ \Longrightarrow\ \HF{B}(\rho)\leq1.
\]
The CHSH counterpart is
$c_B\geq1/2\Rightarrow\mathrm{HB}_A\leq1$ and
$c_A\geq1/2\Rightarrow\mathrm{HB}_B\leq1$,
including equality in Result~1 of~\cite{DSS}.

no_target_yet.statement:
For the family in Eq.~(13) and Fig.~4(b) of~\cite{DSS},
\[
 \omega_p=p|\Psi^-\rangle\langle\Psi^-|+(1-p)|00\rangle\langle00|,
 \qquad |\Psi^-\rangle=(|01\rangle-|10\rangle)/\sqrt2,
\]
the full one-sided optimum is
\begin{equation}
 \HF{A}(\omega_p)=\HF{B}(\omega_p)=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&0\leq p\leq1/2,\\[2pt]
 \displaystyle\sqrt{1+\frac{2(2p-1)^2}{-3p^2+6p-2}},
       &1/2<p\leq1.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
For every $p>0$, the two-sided filtered supremum is $\sqrt3$.
In particular, $0<p\leq1/2$ gives locally AB-inaccessible maximal
hidden $\F$ violation, with ``maximal'' interpreted as a supremum.
For normalized CHSH, one-sided violation occurs exactly for $p>2/3$;
the two-sided supremum is $\sqrt2$ for every $p>0$.
The unfiltered transitions are $p>2/3$ for $\F$ and $p>1/\sqrt2$
for CHSH.

no_target_yet.statement:
For the asymmetric state
$\mu_{\theta,p}=p|\phi_\theta\rangle\langle\phi_\theta|
+(1-p)\rho_A\otimes\id/2$, $0\leq p\leq1$,
\[
 c_B=0,\quad c_A=\frac{z(1-p^2)}{1-p^2z^2},\quad
 \HF{A}(\mu_{\theta,p})=\sqrt3p,\quad
 \mathrm{HB}_A(\mu_{\theta,p})=\sqrt2p.
\]
Consequently $p>1/\sqrt3$ and $c_A\geq2/3$ certify
Alice-accessible, Bob-inaccessible hidden $\F$ violation.
This region is nonempty for each $1/\sqrt3<p<1$ and sufficiently
small positive $\theta$.
Likewise $p>1/\sqrt2$ and $c_A\geq1/2$ certify
Alice-accessible, Bob-inaccessible hidden CHSH violation;
this region is nonempty for every $1/\sqrt2<p<1$.
no_target_yet.title: The F3 threshold is 2/3: the QSE conjecture of Ducuara, Susa and Skrzypczyk (arXiv:2406.03945v1, Section II, p. 3) and extensions of Milne et al. (2014), Mukherjee, Patro and Ganguly (2021), and Morelli et al. (2023)

no_target_yet.statement:
For the symmetric state
$\nu_{\theta,p}=p|\phi_\theta\rangle\langle\phi_\theta|
+(1-p)\rho_A\otimes\rho_B$, both centres equal $z(1-p)$.
Put $v=\cos\theta\sin\theta$,
$J=(1-p)v^2$, $C=pv$ and
$H=v\sqrt{p+(1-p)^2v^2}$. If
\begin{equation}
 z(1-p)\geq2/3,\qquad C^2>2HJ,
\end{equation}
then $\nu_{\theta,p}$ has AB-inaccessible hidden $\F$ violation.
For each $0<p<1/3$ these conditions hold at sufficiently small
positive $\theta$. In particular $p=1/4$, $z=99/100$ is an
explicit example.
The analogous sufficient region for AB-inaccessible hidden CHSH
violation is $z(1-p)\geq1/2$ and $C^2>4HJ$.
For every $0<p<1/2$ this region is nonempty at sufficiently small
positive $\theta$.
